question: Should OpenClaw core sponsor a gateway-owned ACP node runtime after the storage, delivery, reconnect, idempotency, and security-proof blockers are fixed, or should this be split into a design issue first?
rationale: The branch adds a broad core runtime/backend and trust-boundary surface, so implementation correctness alone cannot decide whether this architecture belongs in core now.

options.title: Rework as core runtime
options.body: Require the concrete blockers and real node proof to be fixed on this branch, then do a human storage/security review before merge.

options.title: Split into architecture work
options.body: Close or pause this branch and keep the ACP node runtime as a design/product item until maintainers approve the permanent state and node-command contract.

options.title: Reject core ownership
options.body: Decline the core ACP node runtime direction and route any optional worker experiments outside the main runtime until a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Rework as core runtime
recommendation.body: Require the concrete blockers and real node proof to be fixed on this branch, then do a human storage/security review before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The best available history points to this account on the current ACP dispatch and node-host/gateway surfaces touched by the PR.
